section.heading: 1. Purpose

provision.text: Purpose

provision.label: a.
provision.text: To provide a comprehensive Department of the Navy (DON) policy for handling protest, extremist, and criminal gang activities by Service Members pursuant to the guidance provided by references (a) through (s). See enclosure (1) for a listing of these references.

provision.label: b.

section.heading: 4. Applicability

provision.text: Applicability

provision.label: a.
provision.text: This instruction applies to all DON Service Members, specifically: members of the Active and Reserve Components (RC), as well as midshipmen of the United States (U.S.) Naval Academy and the Naval Reserve Officer Training Corps.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: This instruction does not apply to DON civilian employees. DON civilian employees, as well as Service Members, are subject to reference (c). SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 2

1. Possession and Distribution of Printed and Electronic

provision.text: Possession and Distribution of Printed and Electronic Materials on Installation

provision.label: a.
provision.text: A commander is not authorized to prohibit the distribution of a specific issue of a publication distributed through official outlets such as Navy or Marine Corps exchanges and military libraries. Prohibiting the sale or rental of sexually explicit material on Department of War (DoW) property is governed by reference (i).
A commander may require prior approval of publications to be distributed on a military installation through other than official outlets to determine if the publication would:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Create a clear danger to the loyalty, discipline, or morale of Service Members.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Materially interfere with the accomplishment of the military mission.
Distribution of any publication determined to be a danger in any of the areas in paragraphs 1.a.(1)(a) and 1.a.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: of this enclosure will be prohibited.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: While the mere possession of unauthorized printed material may not be prohibited, printed material that is prohibited from distribution will be impounded if the commander determines that an attempt will be made to distribute it.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: The fact that a publication is critical of government policies or officials is not, in itself, a ground on which distribution may be prohibited.

5. On-Installation Demonstrations and Similar Activities

provision.text: On-Installation Demonstrations and Similar Activities

provision.label: a.
provision.text: The commander of a military installation or other military-controlled facility under the jurisdiction of the U.S. will prohibit any demonstration or activity on the installation or facility that could:
Result in interference with or prevention of orderly accomplishment of the mission of the installation or facility.
Present a clear danger to the loyalty, discipline, or morale of Service Members.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: It is a crime for any person to enter a military reservation for any purpose prohibited by law or lawful regulations, or for any person to enter or re-enter an installation after having been barred by order of the commander pursuant to reference (c). SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 3 Enclosure (3)

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Service Members are prohibited from participating in on- installation demonstrations and similar activities as described under paragraph 5.a. of this enclosure.

section.heading: 7. Grievances. The right of members to complain and request
8. Extremist Activities

provision.text: Extremist Activities

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Extremist activities are inconsistent with the responsibilities and obligations of Military Service, as well as the oaths of office and enlistment, and can be prohibited even in some circumstances in which such activities would be constitutionally protected in a civilian setting. Active participation in extremist activities as defined below is prohibited and, as appropriate, may be punished in the military context for several overlapping, compelling reasons. First, such active participation undermines morale and reduces combat readiness. Second, it calls into question the individual’s ability to follow orders from, or effectively lead and serve with, persons of diverse backgrounds, preventing maximum utilization and development of the DON’s most valuable asset: SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 4 Enclosure (3) its people. Finally, such behavior damages the Nation’s trust and confidence in the DON as an institution and the military as a professional fighting force.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Enforcement of this policy is the responsibility of every commander. It is the commander’s responsibility to maintain good order and discipline in the unit, and every commander has the inherent authority and responsibility to take appropriate actions to accomplish this goal. Active participation in extremist activities (which includes some forms of conduct with respect to groups and organizations that actively participate in extremist activities) does not accord with military values and is not conducive to good order and discipline. Service Members will be held appropriately accountable for active participation in extremist activities, whether in their individual capacity or on behalf of a group.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Service Members are prohibited from actively participating in extremist activities.
Extremist Activities. For the purposes of this instruction, the term “extremist activities” means the following:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Advocating for or engaging in unlawful force, unlawful violence, or other illegal means to deprive individuals of their rights under the U.S. Constitution or the laws of the U.S., including those of any state, commonwealth, territory, or the District of Columbia, or any political subdivision thereof.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Advocating for or engaging in unlawful force or violence to achieve goals that are political, religious, discriminatory, or ideological in nature.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Advocating for, engaging in, or supporting terrorism, within the U.S. or abroad.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Advocating for, engaging in, or supporting the overthrow of the government of the U.S., or any political subdivision thereof, including that of any state, commonwealth, territory, or the District of Columbia, by force or violence; or seeking to alter the form of these governments by unconstitutional or other unlawful means (e.g., sedition). SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 5 Enclosure (3)

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Advocating for or encouraging military, civilian, or contractor personnel within the DoW or U.S. Coast Guard to violate the laws of the U.S., or any political subdivision thereof, including those of any state, commonwealth, territory, or the District of Columbia, or to disobey lawful orders or regulations, for the purpose of disrupting military activities (e.g., subversion), or personally undertaking the same.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Advocating for widespread unlawful discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including pregnancy), or sexual orientation.

Active Participation. For purposes of this paragraph, the term “active participation” means the following, except where such activity is within the scope of an official duty (e.g., intelligence or law enforcement operations):

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Advocating for or engaging in the use or threat of unlawful force or violence in support of extremist activities.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Advocating for, or providing material support or resources to, individuals or organizations that promote or threaten the unlawful use of force or violence in support of extremist activities, with the intent to support such promotion or threats.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Knowingly communicating information that compromises the operational security of any military organization or mission, in support of extremist activities.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: Recruiting or training others to engage in extremist activities.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Fundraising for, or making personal contributions through donations of any kind (including but not limited to the solicitation, collection, or payment of fees or dues) to, a group or organization that engages in extremist activities, with the intent to support those activities.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Creating, organizing, or taking a leadership role in a group or organization that engages in or advocates for extremist activities, with knowledge of those activities. SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 6 Enclosure (3)

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: Actively demonstrating or rallying in support of extremist activities (but not merely observing such demonstrations or rallies as a spectator).

provision.label: (h)
provision.text: Attending a meeting or activity with the knowledge that the meeting or activity involves extremist activities, with the intent to support those activities:
When the nature of the meeting or activity constitutes a breach of law and order.
When a reasonable person would determine the meeting or activity is likely to result in violence.
In violation of off-limits sanctions or other lawful orders.

provision.label: (i)
provision.text: Distributing literature or other promotional materials, on or off a military installation, the primary purpose and content of which is to advocate for extremist activities, with the intent to promote that advocacy.

provision.label: (j)
provision.text: Knowingly receiving material support or resources from a person or organization that advocates or actively participates in extremist activities with the intent to use the material support or resources in support of extremist activities.

provision.label: (k)
provision.text: When using a government communications system and with the intent to support extremist activities, knowingly accessing internet websites or other materials that promote or advocate extremist activities.

provision.label: (l)
provision.text: Knowingly displaying paraphernalia, words, or symbols in support of extremist activities or in support of groups or organizations that support extremist activities, such as flags, clothing, tattoos, and bumper stickers, whether on or off a military installation.

provision.label: (m)
provision.text: Engaging in electronic and cyber activities regarding extremist activities, or groups that support extremist activities – including posting, liking, sharing, re-tweeting, or otherwise distributing content – when such action is taken with SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 7 Enclosure (3) the intent to promote or otherwise endorse extremist activities. Service Members are responsible for the content they publish on all personal and public internet domains, including social media sites, blogs, websites, and applications.

provision.label: (n)
provision.text: Knowingly taking any other action in support of, or engaging in, extremist activities, when such conduct is prejudicial to good order and discipline or is Service- discrediting.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Command Authority and Responsibilities

Commanders have the authority and responsibility to prohibit Service Members from active participation in extremist activities, and other activities that adversely affect good order and discipline within the command. This includes, but is not limited to, the authority to order the removal of symbols, flags, posters, or other displays from military-controlled areas; to place areas or activities off-limits; and to order Service Members not to participate in activities that are contrary to the good order and discipline of the unit, or pose a threat to the health, safety, and security of Service Members or a military installation.

Commanders may, as appropriate, pursue adverse administrative action in addition to or in lieu of punitive action in response to a Service Member’s active participation in extremist activities, pursuant to Military Service regulations and other existing authorities. Adverse administrative action may include involuntary separation, reassignment, loss of security clearance, denial of reenlistment, and other administrative or disciplinary actions deemed appropriate by the commander, based on the specific facts and circumstances of the particular case.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Preventive Activities

Commanders will remain alert for signs of possible future extremist activities. Commanders will intervene early, primarily through counseling, when observing such signs even though the signs may not rise to the level of active participation or threaten good order and discipline, but only suggest such potential. The goal of early intervention is to minimize the risk of future extremist activities. In these SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 8 Enclosure (3) situations, commanders will educate the Service member regarding the potential adverse effects of their actions.

For example, commanders may advise Service Members that extremist activities are inconsistent with the military’s goals, beliefs, and values, as well as the oaths of office and enlistment. Additionally, commanders may advise Service Members that active participation in extremist activities:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: Will be taken into consideration when evaluating duty performance, to include appropriate remarks on evaluation reports.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: Will be taken into consideration when selections for positions of leadership and responsibility or military educational opportunities are made.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: Will result in a report to the appropriate agency for possible revocation of security clearance, which may lead to separation from the Armed Forces.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: May result in reassignment.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: May result in reclassification or bar to reenlistment actions, as appropriate.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Will result in reports to law enforcement and/or counterintelligence authorities, as appropriate, pursuant to enclosure (5).

Commanders will consider all available resources to assist Service Members showing signs of potential involvement in extremist activities, such as command-directed mental health evaluations, financial counseling sessions, etc.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Reporting Requirements. Commanders will remain attentive for signs of extremism involving Service Members in their command, even though the signs may not rise to the level of active participation or threaten good order and discipline, but only suggest such potential. A commander notified of suspected extremist activities will take appropriate actions to investigate and address the allegations in consultation with their first Staff Judge Advocate in the chain of command. SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 9 Enclosure (3)

Upon receipt of any allegation that a Service Member engaged in an activity prohibited under enclosure (3), paragraph 8 of this instruction, commanders will submit timely reporting in connection with all reported allegations pursuant to enclosure (5) of this instruction.

Additionally, where appropriate, commanders will ensure substantiated derogatory information is recorded as an incident report in the personnel system of record, pursuant to reference (o) and applicable Navy or Marine Corps guidance.

section.heading: 9. Criminal Gangs

provision.text: Criminal Gangs

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Service Members must not actively advocate criminal gang doctrine, ideology, or causes.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Service Members are prohibited from active participation in criminal gangs pursuant to reference (p) and in other organizations that advocate criminal gang doctrine, ideology, or causes. Active participation in criminal gangs or organizations is prohibited. Active participation, as applied to such criminal gangs and organizations, includes, but is not limited to, fundraising; demonstrating or rallying; recruiting, training, organizing, or leading members; distributing material (including posting on-line); knowingly wearing gang colors or clothing; having tattoos or body markings associated with such gangs or organizations; or otherwise engaging in activities in furtherance of the objective of such gangs or organizations that are detrimental to good order, discipline, or mission accomplishment or are otherwise incompatible with Military Service.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Commanders have the authority to employ, as appropriate, the full range of administrative and disciplinary actions, including processing for administrative separation or criminal action, against Service Members who engage in prohibited criminal gang activities.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: The functions of command include vigilance about the existence of such activities; active use of investigative authority to include a prompt and fair complaint process; and use of administrative powers such as counseling, reprimands, orders, and performance evaluations to deter such activities. SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 10 Enclosure (3)

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Preventive Activities. Commanders will remain alert for signs of future criminal gang activities. They will intervene early, primarily through counseling, when observing such signs even though the signs may not rise to active advocacy or active participation or may not threaten good order and discipline, but only suggest such potential. The goal of early intervention is to minimize the risk of future criminal gang activities.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Reporting Requirements. Commanders will remain attentive for signs of criminal gang activities involving Service Members in their command, even though the signs may not rise to the level of active participation or threaten good order and discipline, but only suggest such potential. A commander notified of suspected criminal gang activities will take appropriate actions to investigate and address the allegations in consultation with their first Staff Judge Advocate in the chain of command.

Upon receipt of any allegation that a Service Member engaged in a criminal gang activity prohibited under enclosure (3), paragraph 9 of this instruction, commanders will submit timely reporting in connection with all reported allegations pursuant to enclosure (5) of this instruction.

Additionally, where appropriate, commanders will ensure substantiated derogatory information is recorded as an incident report in the personnel system of record, pursuant to reference (e) and applicable Navy or Marine Corps guidance. SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 Enclosure (4) RESPONSIBILITIES

section.heading: 1. The Assistant Secretary of the Navy (Manpower and Reserve

provision.text: The Assistant Secretary of the Navy (Manpower and Reserve Affairs) (ASN (M&RA)) will:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Provide oversight of Navy and Marine Corps policies on handling protest, extremist, and criminal gang activities.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Ensure compliance with the requirements of reference (p) and enclosure (5) of this instruction, including submission of quarterly reports to the SECNAV for forwarding to the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness (OUSW (P&R)) and the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW (I&S)).

section.heading: 2. The Naval Inspector General (NAVINSGEN) and the Inspector

provision.text: The Naval Inspector General (NAVINSGEN) and the Inspector General of the Marine Corps (IGMC) will:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Cooperate with the DoW Deputy IG for Evaluations (DIG (EVAL)) in carrying out responsibilities under reference (p), including in the design of a system of unique identification codes to assign to each allegation. If more than one Sailor or Marine is implicated by an allegation, the identifier will reflect this fact so that each allegation, and the number of Service Members involved, can be tracked without over-reporting the total number of allegations (for example, an allegation that the joint actions of three Service Members constituted active participation in extremist activities might be coded as [Code]- 01, [Code]-02, and [Code]-03).

provision.label: b.
provision.text: To the maximum extent possible, work with the Offices of the Army IG and Air Force IG to ensure that allegations implicating Service Members from multiple Military Services are assigned corresponding identification codes for concurrent tracking.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Coordinate with office of primary responsibility for extremist and criminal gang activity to develop processes and procedures that support reporting requirements for allegations of allegations of extremist and criminal gang activities as set forth in enclosure (5).

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Following coordination with the office of primary responsibility and other stakeholders as necessary, submit SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 2 Enclosure (4) timely reporting of required data related to allegations of extremist and criminal gang activities to the DIG (EVAL), pursuant to enclosure (5) of this instruction, including:
Any allegation that a Service Member engaged in extremist or criminal gang activities under reference (a).
The referral of any such allegation for purposes of investigation or inquiry, to:

provision.label: (a)
provision.text: A military criminal investigative organization.

provision.label: (b)
provision.text: An IG.

provision.label: (c)
provision.text: A military police or security police organization.

provision.label: (d)
provision.text: A military commander.

provision.label: (e)
provision.text: Service Insider Threat Analytic Hub.

provision.label: (f)
provision.text: Another organization or official of the DoW.

provision.label: (g)
provision.text: A civilian law enforcement organization or official.
The referral of the final report of any such investigation or inquiry to a military commander or other appropriate authority for action for each allegation.
The final determination of whether any reported allegation was substantiated.

Any resulting action taken against a Service Member (including judicial, disciplinary, adverse, or corrective administrative action, Insider Threat mitigation, counseling, or no action taken), based on the determination described in enclosure (4), paragraph 2.c.(4) of this instruction.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: On a quarterly basis as described in enclosure (5), submit timely reporting of required data to ASN (M&RA).

section.heading: 3. The Director, Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS),

provision.text: The Director, Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS), will: SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 3 Enclosure (4)

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Initiate, conduct, and direct independent investigations and associated activities related to extremist or criminal gang allegations that fall within the NCIS’s investigative purview consistent with reference (q).

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Establish mechanisms to collect, track, assess, and analyze data and information related to extremist or criminal gang activities and, as appropriate, conduct investigations and associated operations and activities.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: For allegations of extremism or criminal gang activity made directly to the NCIS, notify alleged offender’s command within 72 hours pursuant to enclosure (5).

section.heading: 4. The Chief of Naval Operations and the Commandant of the

provision.text: The Chief of Naval Operations and the Commandant of the Marine Corps, will:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Align Military Service policy to meet the requirements of reference (a) and this instruction pursuant to the following additional provisions:

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Appoint an office of primary responsibility for extremist and criminal gang activity prevention, response, and reporting. This entity will support the NAVINSGEN or the IGMC in managing and meeting reporting requirements under enclosure
of this instruction, including receiving, tracking and consolidating data related to allegations.

provision.label: c.
provision.text: Leadership Message. Issue Service-wide policy statements and use other available mechanisms to visibly promote a consistent top-down leadership message of respect for all individuals and intolerance for extremist behavior.

provision.label: d.
provision.text: Ensure that policy and procedures in this instruction and reference (a) are included in initial active duty training, accessions training, pre-commissioning training, professional military education, commander training, recruiter training, law enforcement personnel training, legal advisor training, and other appropriate Service-training programs.

Senior officer leadership courses, senior enlisted courses, law enforcement training, legal adviser training, and SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 4 Enclosure (4) recruiter training must include recognizing and addressing active participation in extremist activity.
Training must focus on enlisted and officer oaths, the Constitution of the U.S., and our shared ethos, values, and standards, rather than only focusing on prohibited activities.

provision.label: e.
provision.text: Create a policy and checklist mechanism to ensure that all administrative separations of Service Members based on extremist or criminal gang activities are reported to local military law enforcement, the NCIS, Service Insider Threat Analytic Hub, and DoW Consolidated Adjudication Facility.

provision.label: f.
provision.text: Ensure transitioning Service members are provided information during pre-separation counseling on the following:
Potential targeting of veterans by extremist groups.
The means by which to report extremist activities to law enforcement agencies.
Information on reference (e) jurisdiction over retirees.

provision.label: g.
provision.text: Mandate that substantiated allegations are annotated on fitness reports, evaluations, and appropriate Service-level reporting and tracking system(s). The Service-level tracking system will be reviewed for substantiated engagement in extremist or criminal gang activities prior to Service Members’ selection for promotion and other favorable personnel actions.

provision.label: h.
provision.text: Review and standardize accession screening questionnaires to solicit specific information about current or previous extremist activity.

section.heading: 5. Commanders will:

provision.text: Commanders will:

provision.label: a.
provision.text: Ensure a command climate that treats everyone with dignity and respect.

provision.label: b.
provision.text: Ensure a command climate supports the commander’s promulgated guidance that directs all members of the command to be familiar with how to report allegations of extremist or criminal gang activities to ensure a warm handoff to the SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 5 Enclosure (4) appropriate office. The source of reporting may include, but is not limited to, military law enforcement; Service Insider Threat Analytic Hub; counterintelligence or other security officials; military equal opportunity professionals; members of the command's servicing legal office; family advocacy professionals; IG representatives; and individual Service Members or family members.

provision.label: c.

provision.label: f.

section.heading: 1. Reporting Extremist and Criminal Gang Activities

provision.text: Reporting Extremist and Criminal Gang Activities

provision.label: a.
provision.text: An allegation is “received” when it is reported to any member of the chain of command of either the individual who reports the allegation or the alleged offender to a military law enforcement, counter-insider threat, counterintelligence or other security official to a military equal opportunity professional, to a member of the command's servicing legal office, to a family advocacy professional, or to an IG representative.
Allegations within this enclosure refer to reports of extremist and criminal gang activities.

If the recipient of an allegation (for example, a family advocacy professional receiving a restricted report from a victim) is prohibited from conveying an allegation to a commander or other authority due to confidentiality obligations pursuant to established Navy or Marine Corps policy, then the report to the NAVINSGEN or the IGMC will also indicate that no additional reports regarding the allegation are forthcoming, and identify the specific Navy or Marine Corps policy and circumstances that prohibit additional disclosure to the chain of command. The NAVINSGEN or the IGMC will communicate this to DIG (EVAL).

provision.label: b.

Any allegation that a non-senior Service Member engaged in extremist or criminal gang activities will be provided to the immediate commander of the alleged offender within three working days of receipt.

Within three working days following receipt of a non- senior Service Member allegation, the commander will notify the following entities for the purposes of tracking, reporting, investigation and/or inquiry, depending on the entities’ mission and function: SECNAVINST 1610.4A 13 May 2026 2 Enclosure (5)
